reason: E1 and E2 support oxide instability and spallation under wear, but neither addresses corrosion, galvanic coupling, or the synergistic wear-corrosion interaction. E3 is about processing effects on wear and does not support any key premise. The core premises about galvanic coupling and synergistic degradation are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Friction-induced oxide films on HEAs can be mechanically unstable and spall under high-temperature wear
Spallation of the oxide film exposes the underlying alloy and promotes further degradation
Eutectic HEA microstructures contain compositionally distinct phases with different electrochemical activities
Exposed phase boundaries can act as sites for galvanic coupling and localized corrosion
Simultaneous wear and corrosion produce synergistic degradation exceeding the sum of individual effects
